classification.difficultyReason: Justify the supplied angles using the exact sine ratio, the two positive quadrants and repetition after 2π, explaining why these exhaust the stated domain.

content.prompt: Show that the solutions of $\sin\theta=\frac{1}{2}$ in the domain $\theta\in[0,4\pi]$ are $\frac{\pi}{6}$, $\frac{5\pi}{6}$, $\frac{13\pi}{6}$, $\frac{17\pi}{6}$.

answer.short: $\theta=\frac{\pi}{6},\frac{5\pi}{6},\frac{13\pi}{6},\frac{17\pi}{6}$. Sine is positive in quadrants I and II and repeats every $2\pi$.
answer.worked:
The reference angle is $\frac{\pi}{6}$, and sine is positive in quadrants I and II.
$$\begin{align*}\theta&=\frac{\pi}{6},\pi-\frac{\pi}{6}\quad\text{in }[0,2\pi],\\\theta&=\frac{\pi}{6},\frac{5\pi}{6}\quad\text{in }[0,2\pi].\end{align*}$$
Adding $2\pi$ gives the solutions in the next period:
$$\begin{align*}\theta&=\frac{\pi}{6}+2\pi,\frac{5\pi}{6}+2\pi,\\\theta&=\frac{13\pi}{6},\frac{17\pi}{6}.\end{align*}$$
These are the four solutions in $[0,4\pi]$; neither endpoint satisfies the equation.
